findings.title: Member routes pass :id but controller requires :group_id, breaking add/remove member
findings.body: The new routes `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` are declared inside `resources :groups` without a `collection` block, so Rails treats them as member routes: the URL is `/admin/groups/:id/members` and the group id arrives as `params[:id]`. However both `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` and `#remove_member` do `params.require(:group_id)`, which will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` (HTTP 400) for every real request. The JavaScript in `discourse/models/group.js` calls `/admin/groups/<id>/members.json`, matching the member route, so adding or removing a member from the admin UI will always fail. The specs pass because they invoke the controller actions directly with `group_id:` and never exercise the routing. Either wrap the routes in `collection do ... end` (so the client sends `group_id` as a query/body param) or change the controller to use `params[:id]`, and add a request/route-level test.

findings.title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. For a group whose membership is an exact multiple of the page size (e.g. 100 users with limit 50) this yields 3 pages instead of 2. The 'next' button is then enabled on the real last page; clicking it sets `offset = min(offset + limit, user_count)` = user_count, and `findMembers` fetches an empty page, showing the admin a blank member list with pagination '3/3'. The formula should be `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with the zero case already handled).

findings.title: Remove-member link is shown for automatic groups because `automatic` is resolved on the member
findings.body: The item view's context is the member (a User), so `{{#unless automatic}}` looks up `automatic` on the user object, which never has that property — the condition is always true and the remove (×) link is rendered even when viewing an automatic group. The server rejects the removal with a 422, but the admin UI offers an action that can never succeed, and the failed call is silently unhandled (no error callback on `removeMember` in the model). Use `{{#unless view.parentView.automatic}}` (or pass the flag into the view) so the link is hidden for automatic groups.
